
 Usage: openajar connect [OPTIONS] [ssh_host]

 Tunnel to a node, give its agents their own grant, and register it with Claude
 Code. Reads the node's MCP port and its own token over SSH (kept in memory,
 never printed or stored), keeps an SSH tunnel up with launchd (systemd on
 Linux), and asks the node through the tunnel for two credentials: a grant for
 the agents (CLIENT@this-computer, every lane, up to the highest level the node
 allows, revocable per connection) that Claude Code sends, and the owner's
 device credential that `openajar open` and `openajar access approvals` use.
 Both go to the macOS Keychain, in separate items. Safe to run again: a working
 grant and tunnel are kept.

 Claude Code and Codex are registered when installed here, and the openajar
 skills go into Claude Code.

 Codex runs `openajar mcp-bridge NAME`, which reads the same stored token: no
 token in config.toml.

 A host with no node gets one first, after one question (`--install` skips it,
 `--dry-run` shows it).

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   ssh_host      <str>  The node's SSH host, as in ~/.ssh/config (for example │
│                        mynode).                                              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --name               <str>                      Connection name (default:    │
│                                                 from the host). Claude Code  │
│                                                 sees the server as           │
│                                                 openajar-NAME.               │
│ --local-port         <int range> [1<=x<=65535]  Local tunnel port (default   │
│                                                 7400, else the next free     │
│                                                 one).                        │
│ --remote-home        <str>                      OPENAJAR_HOME on the node.   │
│                                                 [default: /var/lib/agentos]  │
│ --token-store        <auto|keychain|file>       Where the credentials are    │
│                                                 kept: keychain (the macOS    │
│                                                 default) or file (chmod 600, │
│                                                 the Linux default).          │
│                                                 [default: auto]              │
│ --ceiling            <str>                      The most the agents' grant   │
│                                                 may do: read, draft, commit  │
│                                                 (publish or send), pay or    │
│                                                 irreversible (default        │
│                                                 commit, or what the          │
│                                                 connection had).             │
│ --agent-ttl          <str>                      How long the agents' grant   │
│                                                 lasts, for example 90d or    │
│                                                 26w (default 90d).           │
│ --client             <str>                      Who uses the grant: its      │
│                                                 subject is                   │
│                                                 CLIENT@this-computer         │
│                                                 (default claude-code).       │
│ --special            <str>                      A special capability for the │
│                                                 agents' grant, for example   │
│                                                 exec or memory (repeatable;  │
│                                                 default memory_read, which   │
│                                                 reads workspace memory and   │
│                                                 never writes it).            │
│ --new-grant                                     Issue a new agent grant and  │
│                                                 revoke the old one.          │
│ --toolsets           <str>                      Which tools the agents list: │
│                                                 toolset names (for example   │
│                                                 files,flows; core is always  │
│                                                 in), full for every tool, or │
│                                                 default for the node's own   │
│                                                 setting (default: what the   │
│                                                 connection had). Agents      │
│                                                 reach the rest with          │
│                                                 tools_more and tools_call.   │
│ --upgrade                                       Move every connection that   │
│                                                 still holds the node token   │
│                                                 to its own grant.            │
│ --remove             NAME                       Remove the connection NAME   │
│                                                 (see `openajar status`):     │
│                                                 revoke its grant, stop its   │
│                                                 tunnel, delete its           │
│                                                 credentials and its Claude   │
│                                                 Code and Codex entries.      │
│ --install                                       If the host has no openajar  │
│                                                 node, install one without    │
│                                                 asking (Ubuntu or Debian,    │
│                                                 root or passwordless sudo).  │
│                                                 A host with a node is never  │
│                                                 touched.                     │
│ --dry-run                                       Print every command connect  │
│                                                 would run on the host, run   │
│                                                 only a read-only check, and  │
│                                                 change nothing.              │
│ --check                                         Check each connection (or    │
│                                                 the one named): the tunnel,  │
│                                                 the grant, and that Claude   │
│                                                 Code and Codex see the       │
│                                                 server.                      │
│ --no-claude                                     Leave Claude Code (and its   │
│                                                 skills) alone.               │
│ --no-codex                                      Leave Codex's config.toml    │
│                                                 alone.                       │
│ --no-skills                                     Do not copy the openajar     │
│                                                 skills into Claude Code.     │
│ --by-hand                                       Print the tunnel, grant and  │
│                                                 `claude mcp add` steps to do │
│                                                 yourself (run it on the      │
│                                                 node), and change nothing.   │
│ --help                                          Show this message and exit.  │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Your connections: `openajar status`. Remove one: `openajar connect --remove
 NAME`. The steps by hand: `openajar connect --by-hand`, on the node.
